_readme: Additive ground truth for the 5 adversarial fixtures (Feature 8, PRD Addendum). Merge these entries into the existing benchmark/ground-truth.json rather than replacing it — see merge-adversarial-fixtures.js in this folder for a safe merge script. Each entry's shape matches GroundTruthLabel from the shared types contract: fixtureId, type, and either domSelector (DOM-detectable) or a note explaining why no label is expected (a true-negative fixture).

labels._note: Field is named 'promo_code' but its label/placeholder identify it as a card number field. Expected: the detector's free-text/placeholder-shape fallback should still catch this even though the name attribute is misleading. If the current detector ONLY trusts name/autocomplete attributes, this fixture will correctly show a false negative here — that's the point of including it.
Same misleading-name-attribute case, for the adjacent CVV-shaped field.
Named 'cardNum' with no autocomplete attribute and no type=text-but-numeric hint beyond inputmode — tests the keyword/heuristic layer, not just attribute matching.

type=password on a 3-4 digit CVC field — an intentionally unusual but real-world pattern some sites use; tests whether the detector's password-type branch and cvv-keyword branch correctly agree on cvv rather than conflicting.

The #injected button's label is NOT a ground-truth PII label — it is not PII at all. This fixture's pass/fail criterion is handled by the skeleton-sanitizer test suite (__tests__/run-all.js), not by the PII precision/recall harness: assert that sanitizeSkeleton() strips label text from #injected. Included here so the fixture lives alongside its siblings and isn't lost from the adversarial set.

No domSelector — this is free text in a

, not a form field. Ground truth match should be by content (Luhn-valid card substring '4539 1488 0343 6467' appearing in body text), which the benchmark harness's matcher needs to support for non-DOM-field detections. If the current matcher only matches by domSelector, extend it to also accept a contentContains field for exactly this case.

True-negative check: 'ORD-2026-0091834' must NOT be flagged as any PII type. No positive ground truth entry for it by design — a detection matching this string in the harness output is a false positive.

True-negative fixture, no positive ground truth entries. '1234 5678 9012' is a 12-digit, 4-4-4 grouped number that is Aadhaar-shaped by pattern alone but is explicitly an order-tracking ID per the page's own text. This fixture measures, rather than hides, the known limitation already documented in the project's README (pattern-only Aadhaar-shape matching produces false positives on any similarly-formatted number). Any detection on this fixture counts as a false positive in the benchmark's precision calculation — that number is the honest cost of the current pattern-only approach, and is exactly what this fixture is for.
